record.detail: The Crime Suppression Division arrested a Chinese national at a condo in Nong Prue who allegedly ran a network rotating bank accounts and ATM cards to launder scam proceeds of about 1.8 million yuan (about 8.8 million baht).

record.title: Finance ministry plans gold-trade oversight to trace grey money
record.detail: The Fiscal Policy Office said it would link financial and gold transaction data, with the BoT and AMLO, to trace money flows into bullion, noting no agency directly regulates the gold business.

record.title: Ayutthaya abbot arrested over alleged embezzlement and laundering of temple funds
record.detail: The CIB arrested the abbot of Wat Phutthaisawan, accused of diverting over 92 million baht in temple funds with unauthorised donation receipts, on charges including money laundering; a female associate was detained for questioning.

record.title: Government says nominee registrations down 81.77%, 20bn baht seized or frozen
record.detail: Officials said high-risk nominee registrations fell 81.77% in a year, about 14,000 companies and 5,800 land plots are under investigation, and AMLO has seized or frozen 20.392 billion baht, Thai Examiner reported.

record.title: Temple fund case sent to AMLO as police eye third parties
record.detail: The Crime Suppression Division forwarded documents on over 215 million baht in transactions in the Wat Phutthaisawan fund case to AMLO and said one or two third parties may be involved.

record.title: Chinese USDT supplier to scam laundering network arrested in Chiang Mai
record.detail: The CIB and Anti-Online Scam Centre arrested a Chinese man in Chiang Mai accused of supplying USDT to a laundering network, with wallets showing 7.2 million USDT (about 238 million baht) linked to at least 16 fraud cases; a car, luxury watch and cash were seized.

record.title: Alleged head of 'PAOFENG' gambling payment network arrested near Pattaya
record.detail: The CIB arrested a Chinese national said to lead the PAOFENG network, which allegedly used over 6,000 Alipay and WeChat accounts to collect bets and moved about 900 million baht, partly via crypto; he faces deportation to China.

record.title: DSI recommends indicting 34, including an MP, over forex scheme with laundering charges
record.detail: DSI recommended indicting 34 suspects, including a sitting MP and an actor-politician, for public fraud, unlicensed securities trading and money laundering over a forex scheme that allegedly took 1 billion baht from 500 victims; 65 million baht was seized, Thai Enquirer reported.

record.title: 25 Myanmar migrants found in cargo van after chase in Nakhon Sawan
record.detail: Highway police said a Thai driver fled into forest after being stopped on Highway 122 and 25 undocumented Myanmar nationals were found in the enclosed cargo box; police said migrants had paid brokers about 20,000 baht each.
record.place: Highway 122 km 12, Nakhon Sawan Tok subdistrict

record.title: Russian accused of leading extortion gang arrested on Koh Samui
record.detail: Immigration police said they arrested a Russian national wanted for allegedly extorting about 1 million roubles from a Russian car dealership executive by threatening to leak confidential information.
record.attribution: Surat Thani Immigration Police / Immigration Bureau

record.title: Dice gambling den raided in Nong Prue, 31 arrested
record.detail: District officers and police raided a gambling den and arrested 31 people, seizing cash, betting boards and CCTV equipment; one woman was hospitalised with heart symptoms.
record.agency: Bang Lamung District Office / Royal Thai Police

record.title: Foreigner-only poker game raided at Rawai villa
record.detail: Chalong police said they raided a villa poker game advertised on Instagram to foreigners and arrested nine foreign nationals (7 Russian, 1 Ukrainian, 1 Kazakh) under the Gambling Act.

record.title: Highway police stop pickup carrying 7 Myanmar migrants
record.detail: Highway police said a 36-year-old Myanmar driver was transporting seven undocumented Myanmar nationals from Nakhon Sawan to Bangkok for 1,000 baht each; police said the migrants had entered via Mae Sot.
record.place: Phahonyothin Road km 38-39, Khlong Nueng subdistrict

record.title: Two Indian men arrested for forcing Indian women into prostitution
record.detail: Pattaya police said two Indian men (25 and 32) lured three Indian women with fake restaurant jobs, took their passports and forced them into street prostitution in February before the women escaped and reported.

record.title: Warehouse raid seizes over 120,000 fake cosmetics
record.detail: Consumer Protection Police said they seized 122,872 counterfeit toothpaste and skincare products worth over 6 million baht and arrested a Chinese national caretaker; the owner was being sought.

record.title: DSI raids department-store storage, seizes 20m baht fake goods
record.detail: DSI said it executed 17 search warrants on counterfeit storage at a Bangkok department store, seizing fake branded clothing and bags estimated at 20 million baht.

record.title: Phuket immigration police bust South Korean drug export gang
record.detail: Immigration police said four South Korean nationals aged 31-43 were arrested with about 300 g ketamine and 100 g crystal meth, acting on information from South Korean police about exports to Korea.

record.title: 11 South Koreans arrested at Ram Inthra call-centre house
record.detail: CIB said its technology crime division raided a luxury house used as a call-centre base, arresting 11 South Koreans who allegedly impersonated prosecutors to defraud Korean victims; over 40 computers and phones were seized.

record.title: Cocaine network dismantled after Silom arrest
record.detail: Police said four suspects (Nigerian, Swiss and two Thai nationals) were arrested in Bangkok and Nonthaburi, seizing about 30 g cocaine and over 2.5 million baht cash.
record.agency: Metropolitan Police Bureau / Narcotics Suppression Bureau

record.title: 16 Cambodian migrants intercepted crossing border
record.detail: Burapha Task Force said it intercepted 16 Cambodian nationals who had paid smugglers 7,500 baht each to cross via a natural route.

record.title: Smuggled fuel bound for Myanmar seized in Tak
record.detail: Rangers and customs said they seized about 840 litres of fuel in Tha Song Yang and 16,000 litres of diesel worth over 700,000 baht in Mae Sot, suspected for export to Myanmar.
record.place: Mae Sot / Ban Mae Salit Luang

record.title: 63 Myanmar migrants found in Phayao safe house
record.detail: A multi-agency team said 63 Myanmar nationals, including three minors, were found in a safe house after entering via Mae Sai and paying brokers 8,500-10,000 baht each.

record.title: Border Patrol Police seize 6 million meth pills in Mae Chan
record.detail: Border Patrol Police said they intercepted an SUV carrying about 6 million meth pills in 20 sacks and arrested three suspects from local highland communities.

record.title: Ivory network raided across seven provinces
record.detail: CIB and national parks officials said raids at 11 locations seized about 180 kg of ivory plus hawksbill turtle and stingray parts worth about 9.9 million baht, arresting nine suspects.
record.place: 11 locations in Samut Sakhon, Uthai Thani, Kamphaeng Phet, Chumphon, Songkhla, Chonburi, Chanthaburi
record.agency: CIB / Natural Resources and Environmental Crime Division / DNP

record.title: 24 Thais stopped crossing to Cambodia to open mule accounts
record.detail: Rangers said they intercepted 24 Thai nationals allegedly recruited for 25,000 baht each to open bank accounts for criminal networks in Cambodia.

record.title: Online gambling site admin arrested in Ranong
record.detail: CCIB said it arrested a 24-year-old woman working as customer service admin for gambling website AM 08, which allegedly had 36,000 members and over 72 million baht annual turnover.

record.title: 16 Chinese arrested at villa poker den
record.detail: Immigration and tourist police said they raided a villa poker den, arresting 16 Chinese nationals and seizing about 100,000 baht cash and chips worth several million baht.
record.place: Soi Mab Yai Lia, Nong Prue subdistrict

record.title: 130 kg of ivory seized on Mekong near Lao border
record.detail: The DNP wildlife division said it seized 22 ivory sections (130.9 kg) and 29 kg of animal remains after a tip-off about smuggling into Laos; suspects escaped.
record.place: Ban Mueang Mi Yai, Mueang Mi subdistrict
record.agency: DNP Wildlife and Flora Protection Division
record.attribution: Wildlife and Flora Protection Division director

record.title: Two money-mule suspects arrested in Chiang Rai over investment scam
record.detail: CCIB said two suspects aged 23 and 24 were arrested on warrants for allegedly supporting a fake gold-trading scam that cost a government official about 2.7 million baht.

record.title: 1.08 million meth pills seized near Mekong in Loei
record.detail: Army-led forces said they seized over 1.08 million meth pills, a pickup and a long-tail boat; suspects fled across the Mekong into Laos.

record.title: Malaysian man caught with 251 live animals at Suvarnabhumi
record.detail: Customs said a 34-year-old Malaysian bound for Kolkata was caught with 251 live animals including hornbills, iguanas, skinks and turtles worth about 600,000 baht.

record.title: Rosewood poachers caught felling trees behind Sri Racha harbour
record.detail: District and forest officials said two men were caught with felled Siamese rosewood (Pterocarpus macrocarpus) logs and chainsaws after residents reported night-time logging.
record.agency: Sri Racha District Office / Chonburi Forest Protection Unit

record.title: Tiger skins and pangolin scales seized at That Phanom shop
record.detail: Environmental crime police said a shop fronting as a souvenir/traditional medicine store held over 100 wildlife items including tiger and clouded leopard skins and pangolin scales, allegedly smuggled from Laos; a 37-year-old Thai woman was arrested.
record.agency: Natural Resources and Environmental Crime Suppression Division

record.title: Chinese-run illegal e-waste yard inspected in Samut Sakhon
record.detail: Officials said about 3,274 cubic metres of e-waste was found at an unlicensed Chinese-operated site and charges were filed under the Factory Act.

record.title: Chinese student rescued from scam-staged 'virtual kidnapping'
record.detail: Police said a 21-year-old Chinese student was coerced by scammers into staging her own kidnapping in Thailand; about HK$1.4m had been paid and HK$3m more demanded before police found her.

record.title: Former couple arrested over child sex trafficking at Sattahip karaoke bar
record.detail: AHTD said a couple aged 43 and 37 with prior trafficking arrests allegedly used a karaoke bar to prostitute 15-year-old girls.

record.title: 11 foreigners and Thai stopped crossing from Poipet
record.detail: Military said 11 people (7 Bangladeshi, 2 Vietnamese, 1 Chinese, 1 Thai) crossed illegally after fleeing unpaid online-business jobs in Poipet, paying smugglers 8,000 baht each.
record.place: Ban Ang Sila, Non Mak Mun subdistrict

record.title: CCIB raids World Cup online betting network, 12 arrested
record.detail: CCIB said coordinated raids on the All Game 248 platform in Bangkok, Samut Prakan and Tak led to 12 arrests and seizure/freezing of assets over 13 million baht.

record.title: Boxing camp manager arrested, 15 children rescued from sex trafficking
record.detail: CIB anti-trafficking police said 15 children aged 13-16 were rescued from a Rayong boxing camp allegedly used for child sex trafficking; a 28-year-old manager was arrested in Chonburi.

record.title: 9.56 million meth pills seized at Saraburi shelter
record.detail: Metropolitan police said they tracked a drug gang using vans and seized 9.56 million meth pills worth over 500 million baht, arresting two men aged 30 and 45.

record.title: 2.45 million illicit cigarettes and guns seized in Pattani
record.detail: ISOC Region 4 said a raid seized 2,452,680 illegal cigarettes, three handguns and about 18.8 million baht cash, detaining three people.
record.srcname: Tobacco Control Research and Knowledge Management Center

record.title: 109 padauk logs seized from two trucks in Chiang Rai
record.detail: National parks officials said two trucks carrying 109 freshly cut padauk logs were stopped and two drivers arrested, following a probe into an illegal timber factory in Mueang Chiang Rai.
record.agency: DNP with CIB, DSI, Highway Police
record.attribution: DNP / Natural Resources and Environment Minister

record.title: CIB 'Blocklist Hunt' seizes 1m pills and 514 kg crystal meth
record.detail: CIB said a week-long operation (4-11 Sept) arrested 16 people including alleged network figures, seizing over 1 million meth pills, 514 kg crystal meth, vehicles and guns worth over 120 million baht.
record.place: Bueng Kan, Khon Kaen (Kranuan, Nong Kung Si) and others

record.title: Ratchaburi karaoke bar raided over child sex trafficking
record.detail: Anti-trafficking police said three women (49, 38, 26) were arrested for allegedly offering girls under 15 for sex at a karaoke bar.

record.title: 58,000 meth pills and guns seized at Roi Et safe house
record.detail: Region 4 police said they seized 57,934 meth pills, three illegal guns and assets over 1 million baht, arresting two at the scene and more than 10 network members; police alleged supply from a Lao national.
record.place: Ban Nong Phra Bang, Kamphaeng subdistrict

record.title: 2.7 million meth pills found stashed in Chiang Dao
record.detail: Pha Muang Force and Border Patrol Police said a night patrol found 2.7 million meth pills in 10 backpacks near Ban Rin Luang; no arrests were reported.
record.agency: Pha Muang Force / Border Patrol Police 335

record.title: Bang Bon mansion raided as Japan-targeting scam base
record.detail: Immigration police said 14 people (Japanese, Chinese, Myanmar, Taiwanese and Thai) were arrested at a mansion used to impersonate Japanese police, seizing fake uniforms, badges, 27 phones and ketamine.
record.place: Soi Ekkachai 112, Bang Bon Nuea subdistrict

record.title: DOPA raids two Chiang Mai gambling dens, over 100 held
record.detail: DOPA said raids on two dens in Mueang Chiang Mai detained over 100 gamblers and 14 alleged organisers, seizing over 2 million baht in cash and chips; rental documents were reportedly linked to local politicians.

record.title: Three Chinese women rescued from ransom house near Pattaya
record.detail: Immigration and police said they rescued three Chinese women allegedly confined, assaulted and held for ransom by Chinese men; four were detained and two escaped.

record.title: Excise officials among 3 arrested in phone-shop kidnapping sting
record.detail: Samut Prakan police said men posing as excise officers abducted a shop manager and a Myanmar worker demanding ransom; three including two Excise Department officials were arrested in a sting and four remain at large.

record.title: Virologist warns of mutated H3N2 flu strain
record.detail: A Chulalongkorn University virologist warned that an A/H3N2 'K' variant with HA1 mutations was spreading and may partly evade immunity and reduce vaccine efficacy, while saying severity had not increased.
record.agency: Chulalongkorn University Centre of Excellence in Clinical Virology
record.attribution: According to a Chulalongkorn virologist, as reported by Thaiger

record.title: BMA asks for work-from-home as red PM2.5 forecast
record.detail: The BMA forecast red-level PM2.5 in Bangkok for 12-15 January and asked agencies and firms to let staff work from home on 12-13 January; a low-emission zone restricting large trucks covered all 50 districts.
record.attribution: According to the BMA, as reported by The Nation

record.title: DDC steps up mpox monitoring in tourist provinces
record.detail: The DDC said Thailand had logged about 1,000 mpox cases since 2022 and was intensifying surveillance in tourist provinces, prioritising vaccine for Bangkok, Chon Buri, Chiang Mai and Phuket.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by The Nation

record.title: First rabies death of 2026 in Rayong
record.detail: The DDC said a migrant worker in Rayong died of rabies on 25 January after an untreated puppy bite in December 2025, Thailand's first confirmed rabies death of the year.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Red-level PM2.5 in eastern Bangkok from crop burning
record.detail: Bangkok's average PM2.5 reached 55.6 µg/m³, with Nong Chok at 80.8, Min Buri 77.3 and Khlong Sam Wa 76.5; officials linked it to about 13,000 rai of farm burning in neighbouring provinces.
record.attribution: According to Bangkok Air Quality Center data, as reported by Thaiger

record.title: Bangkok urges WFH as four districts hit red
record.detail: The BMA requested work-from-home on 29-30 January as Nong Chok, Min Buri, Khlong Sam Wa and Khan Na Yao reached red-level PM2.5 and more than 35 districts were orange.
record.attribution: According to the BMA, as reported by The Nation

record.title: PM2.5 exceeds standard in 18 provinces
record.detail: CAPM said PM2.5 exceeded the standard in 18 provinces at 17:00, with peaks of 64.6 µg/m³ in the central/western region, 50.3 in the Northeast and 46.4 in the North.
record.attribution: According to CAPM, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Northeast PM2.5 peaks at 84.9 µg/m³
record.detail: CAPM reported the highest reading of 84.9 µg/m³ in the Northeast, four Bangkok-area stations above standard (up to 48.0), and 22 provinces including Khon Kaen and Udon Thani under close watch.
record.attribution: According to CAPM, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Streptococcus suis: 49 cases, 3 deaths
record.detail: The DDC recorded 49 Streptococcus suis cases in 28 provinces and 3 deaths from 1 January to 10 February, led by Nakhon Ratchasima, Phrae, Chon Buri, Chaiyaphum and Surin, and warned against raw pork.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Chiang Mai among world's most polluted cities
record.detail: IQAir ranked Chiang Mai the third most polluted major city globally, with a US AQI above 150 ('unhealthy'), driven by PM2.5 from crop and forest burning.

record.title: Influenza 137,276 cases, 8 deaths
record.detail: The DDC counted 137,276 flu cases and 8 deaths from 1 January to 9 March, with 15,041 hospitalised; Phayao, Lampang, Phitsanulok, Chiang Mai and Ubon Ratchathani had the highest rates.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Heat index forecast to exceed 52°C
record.detail: The government warned the heat index could top 52°C ('very dangerous') in April-May, with the North, Northeast and Central regions most at risk; 21 heat-related deaths were recorded in 2025.
record.attribution: According to a government spokeswoman, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Chiang Mai ranked world's most polluted city
record.detail: IQAir said Chiang Mai ranked the most polluted major city in the world on 26 March, with a US AQI above 220 from seasonal biomass burning.

record.title: Nine provinces on red PM2.5 alert; Li hits 198.3
record.detail: The Department of Health put Nan, Phayao, Lampang, Lamphun, Chiang Rai, Chiang Mai, Phrae, Mae Hong Son and Nakhon Phanom on red alert; the peak was 198.3 µg/m³ in Li subdistrict, Lamphun, and over 55% of those exposed reported symptoms.
record.attribution: According to the Department of Health, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Chiang Mai faces week of orange-level haze
record.detail: Chiang Mai and northern provinces were forecast to have orange-level PM2.5 from 29 March to 4 April; the provincial health office expanded clean-air rooms to 2,004 sites and sent mobile medical units.
record.agency: Chiang Mai Provincial Public Health Office
record.attribution: According to Chiang Mai health officials, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Northern PM2.5 peaks at 326.3 µg/m³
record.detail: CAPM reported a northern peak of 326.3 µg/m³ with 14 provinces including Chiang Rai, Chiang Mai, Mae Hong Son, Tak and Nakhon Sawan at red level, and 1,971 hotspots nationwide on 1 April.
record.attribution: According to CAPM, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Chiang Mai city PM2.5 near 98 µg/m³
record.detail: Chiang Mai Municipality measured 98.1 µg/m³ PM2.5 at 11:00 (AQI 181); the provincial health office advised cutting outdoor activity and wearing N95 masks.
record.agency: Chiang Mai Provincial Public Health Office
record.attribution: As reported by Chiang Rai Times

record.title: Chiang Mai declared haze disaster zone
record.detail: The Interior Ministry declared Chiang Mai, Lamphun and Phayao disaster zones over wildfire haze to unlock emergency funds; Chiang Mai recorded 131 µg/m³ PM2.5 that afternoon.
record.attribution: According to the Interior Ministry, as reported by Thaiger

record.title: Nine Phayao districts declared disaster areas
record.detail: The Interior Ministry declared disaster assistance zones in 17 districts over wildfire haze: seven in Chiang Mai, Li in Lamphun and nine in Phayao, including Mueang Phayao, Chun and Chiang Kham.
record.attribution: According to the Interior Ministry, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Food poisoning 39,233, diarrhoea 274,151
record.detail: Surveillance data showed 39,233 food poisoning cases and 274,151 acute diarrhoea cases (2 deaths) from 1 January to 17 March, plus 36 heat-related illness cases, as hot weather raised risks.
record.attribution: According to Digital Disease Surveillance data, as reported by The Nation

record.title: PM2.5 exceeds standard in 39 provinces
record.detail: CAPM said 39 provinces exceeded the standard, with northern readings of 56.7-228.8 µg/m³ and the Northeast up to 196.4, while Bangkok and the South were in the good range.
record.attribution: According to CAPM, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Melioidosis 732 cases, 23 deaths
record.detail: The government warned about melioidosis after 732 cases and 23 deaths from 1 January to 16 April; Health Region 7 (Khon Kaen) had 68 cases and 2 deaths.
record.attribution: According to a government spokesperson, as reported by Khaosod English

record.title: Worker dies in fall, suspected heatstroke
record.detail: A municipal waterworks employee died after falling from a bamboo tree in Hat Tha Sao, Chainat, during extreme heat; medics suspected heatstroke or an underlying condition.
record.attribution: According to police and medics, as reported by Khaosod English

record.title: Nan's Huai Khon records 132 µg/m³
record.detail: The Pollution Control Department recorded 132.0 µg/m³ in Huai Khon, Nan, the national peak; 38 provinces exceeded the standard and eight northern provinces were hazardous.
record.attribution: According to the PCD, as reported by Khaosod English

record.title: Two new mpox clade Ib cases
record.detail: The DDC reported two mpox clade Ib cases in Thai men during weeks 18-19, bringing 2026 clade Ib cases to six, and stepped up surveillance.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by The Nation

record.title: No hantavirus outbreak; screening increased
record.detail: After a WHO alert on a cruise-ship cluster, the government said Thailand had no confirmed hantavirus outbreak and increased screening at entry points.
record.attribution: According to a government spokesperson, as reported by Khaosod English

record.title: Hantavirus listed as dangerous disease
record.detail: The National Communicable Disease Committee made hantavirus Thailand's 14th dangerous communicable disease, requiring reports within three hours and 42-day quarantine for high-risk contacts.
record.attribution: According to the NCDC, as reported by Khaosod English

record.title: 21-day quarantine for DRC arrivals over Ebola
record.detail: The DDC ordered 21-day facility quarantine for arrivals from the DR Congo and observation for Uganda arrivals; 10 arrivals screened by 22 May all tested negative.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by The Nation

record.title: NB.1.8.1 becomes dominant Covid variant
record.detail: The DDC reported 3,642 Covid cases and 1 death from 1 January to 23 May, with NB.1.8.1 in 50.95% of samples; cases were rising but below the five-year median.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Influenza tops 170,000 cases, 16 deaths
record.detail: The DDC counted 171,731 flu cases and 16 deaths as of 28 May, with outbreaks starting in schools, workplaces and transport; influenza B was predominant.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by The Nation

record.title: DDC rainy-season disease warning
record.detail: The DDC warned of rainy-season respiratory infections, leptospirosis, melioidosis, hand-foot-mouth disease, dengue, chikungunya, Zika, snakebite and poisonous mushrooms, and activated teams in 12 regional offices.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Rabid dog in Korat; 20 animal cases this year
record.detail: A stray dog in Chai Mongkhon tested positive on 1 June. Nakhon Ratchasima had 20 rabid animals and 1 human death from 1 January to 2 June, with 144 people exposed.
record.agency: Nakhon Ratchasima Provincial Public Health Office
record.attribution: According to provincial health officials, as reported by Khaosod English

record.title: Two die after eating wild mushrooms
record.detail: Two men from Mok Cham Pae died (27 May-2 June) after eating foraged mushrooms suspected to be death caps; the provincial health office warned against unknown mushrooms.
record.agency: Mae Hong Son Provincial Public Health Office
record.attribution: According to provincial health officials, as reported by Thaiger

record.title: 147 Yasothon kindergarten pupils fall ill
record.detail: 147 pupils at a municipal school in Yasothon had vomiting and diarrhoea in suspected food poisoning, and about 15 were treated at Yasothon Hospital; the school closed 12-13 June for disinfection.
record.attribution: According to provincial officials, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Liver fluke in a third of screened students
record.detail: Screening found liver fluke in 4,233 of 12,700+ new Mahasarakham University students and 380 of 1,922 at Rajabhat Maha Sarakham; officials blamed raw pla ra in som tam.
record.agency: Maha Sarakham Provincial Public Health Office
record.attribution: According to provincial health officials, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Mpox reaches 139 cases, 2 deaths
record.detail: The DDC recorded 139 mpox cases (88 clade Ib) and 2 deaths from 1 January to 18 July, mainly in Bangkok, nearby provinces and tourist areas.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by Thaiger

record.title: Leptospirosis 2,190 cases, 30 deaths
record.detail: The DDC reported 2,190 leptospirosis cases and 30 deaths from 1 January to 21 July, highest in the South and Northeast.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Melioidosis 1,654 cases, 77 deaths
record.detail: The DDC reported 1,654 melioidosis cases and 77 deaths (4.66% fatality) from 1 January to 21 July, highest in the South and Northeast.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Border surveillance over Yangon cholera
record.detail: The DDC tightened screening at entry points and border health facilities after a cholera outbreak in Yangon; no Thai cases were reported and public risk was assessed as low.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Dengue 21,620 cases, 31 deaths
record.detail: The DDC recorded 21,620 dengue cases and 31 deaths from 1 January to 19 August, including 1,785 cases and 4 deaths in Bangkok, below last year's levels.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by Thaiger

record.title: Covid cases near 100,000, severity stable
record.detail: The DDC reported 99,691 Covid cases and 15 deaths from 1 January to 31 August; Bangkok, Chonburi and Phuket had the highest rates, and NB.1.8.1 was dominant.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by The Nation

record.title: Hand, foot and mouth disease 53,362 cases
record.detail: The DDC recorded 53,362 HFMD cases, 5,408 hospitalisations and 1 death from 1 January to 1 September, clustered in schools and childcare centres.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by Thaiger

record.title: August flu 87,770 cases; Covid at 135,667
record.detail: The DDC reported 87,770 flu cases in August (57 deaths given) and 135,667 Covid cases with 26 deaths by 15 September; Chonburi, Bangkok and Phuket had the highest Covid rates.
record.attribution: According to the DDC, as reported by The Nation

record.title: 335 mushroom poisonings in lower Northeast
record.detail: ODPC Region 9 reported 335 mushroom poisoning cases and 1 death from January to 21 September: 188 cases and the death in Chaiyaphum, 65 in Surin, 58 in Buriram and 24 in Nakhon Ratchasima.
record.agency: Office of Disease Prevention and Control Region 9
record.attribution: According to ODPC Region 9, as reported by Khaosod English

record.title: 47 Suvarnabhumi flights cancelled over Middle East unrest
record.detail: Khaosod English reported 47 cancellations at Suvarnabhumi on 2 March and 108 between 28 Feb and 2 Mar, by eight airlines, attributed to Middle East unrest; the airport said no passengers were stranded.
record.attribution: Per Suvarnabhumi Airport via Khaosod English

record.title: Phuket runway closed after hard landing; 165 flights hit
record.detail: The Nation reported an Air India Express hard landing disabled the aircraft and closed Phuket's runway until a targeted 21:00 reopening; AOT said 165 flights across four airports were affected.
record.attribution: Flight figures per AOT via The Nation

record.title: Planned MEA power cuts in east Bangkok and Nonthaburi
record.detail: Thairath English relayed an MEA notice of planned maintenance outages on Suwinthawong Road, Bangkok (8:30–15:30) and Rattanathibet Road, Nonthaburi (8:00–14:00).
record.attribution: Planned outage per MEA notice via Thairath

record.title: Battery truck fire damages Burapha Withi Expressway
record.detail: An InterRisk Asia review said a truck carrying lithium-ion batteries caught fire and exploded near km 40 of Highway 34, with the heat damaging the elevated Burapha Withi Expressway above; no deaths were reported.
record.place: Theparat Road (Highway 34) near km 40, under Burapha Withi Expressway

record.title: Chao Phraya Dam release to rise; 7 provinces warned
record.detail: The Nation reported Regional Irrigation Office 12 planned discharge of 500–700 m3/s, raising downstream levels about 1–1.5 m while staying below banks.
record.attribution: Per RID Regional Irrigation Office 12 via The Nation

record.title: Heavy-rain warning; national reservoirs at 56%
record.detail: The Nation reported TMD warned of heavy rain 8–14 June; officials said national reservoirs held 56% and the four main Chao Phraya dams 53% of capacity.
record.attribution: Storage figures per officials via The Nation

record.title: Planned MEA power cuts in Bangkok and Samut Prakan
record.detail: Thairath English relayed an MEA notice of maintenance and undergrounding outages at several Bangkok sites and one in Samut Prakan, mostly between 8:30 and 15:30.
record.place: Multiple sites incl. Chalerm Phrakiat R.9 Soi 28, Sukhumvit Soi 62
record.attribution: Planned outage per MEA notice via Thairath

record.title: RID warns 7 provinces of higher Chao Phraya Dam flow
record.detail: The Nation reported RID expected dam discharge to rise to 500–700 m3/s, lifting downstream levels about 1–1.5 m, with 936 m3/s measured at station C.2.

record.title: Suvarnabhumi postpones 7-month terminal road lane closures
record.detail: The Nation reported Suvarnabhumi cancelled lane closures on its elevated terminal road, planned for 31 Aug 2026–7 Apr 2027 for expansion-joint repairs, after criticism over high-season timing; a new schedule is pending.
record.attribution: Per Suvarnabhumi Airport via The Nation

record.title: Internet connectivity drop detected in Pathum Thani (low confidence)
record.detail: Voidly logged an IODA-detected connectivity drop in the Pathum Thani region from 12:30 UTC; it rated confidence moderate and corroboration low, with no networks named.

record.title: Planned MEA power cuts across Bangkok, Nonthaburi, Samut Prakan
record.detail: Thairath English relayed an MEA notice of planned outages at 12 locations for maintenance and undergrounding, including one overnight Bangkok outage to 01:30 on 17 September.
record.place: Multiple sites incl. Ramkhamhaeng, Phahonyothin, Bang Pu
record.attribution: Planned outage per MEA notice via Thairath

record.title: RID flood alert for 11 Chao Phraya basin provinces
record.detail: The Nation reported RID planned Chao Phraya Dam discharge of 700–1,000 m3/s, with levels up 0.6–1.5 m and Ayutthaya areas outside embankments most at risk.

record.title: Chao Phraya Dam release raised to 1,000–1,300 m3/s
record.detail: The Nation reported RID would raise discharge from about 990 to 1,000–1,300 m3/s after heavy northern rain, warning of a 0.5–1.5 m rise downstream.

record.title: DDPM puts 10 provinces on watch as Chao Phraya rises
record.detail: Chiang Rai Times reported DDPM alerted 10 central provinces including Bangkok, citing Chao Phraya Dam releases of 700–1,000 m3/s and Ayutthaya's Sena, Bang Ban and Bang Pa-in as high-risk.
record.agency: Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation
record.attribution: Per DDPM via Chiang Rai Times

record.title: RID to raise Chao Phraya Dam release to 1,500–2,000 m3/s
record.detail: The Nation reported RID planned releases of 1,500–2,000 m3/s ahead of heavy rain on 23–27 Sept, warning 11 provinces and of rises of 0.7–1.7 m outside embankments in Ayutthaya and Ang Thong.

record.title: Armed gang robs gold shop in Narathiwat mall
record.detail: Khaosod English reported an armed gang robbed a gold shop inside a shopping mall in Narathiwat and one officer was injured; the army linked the heist to insurgent funding and the defence minister said BRN carried it out (per Thai Examiner, 7 Oct).
record.attribution: outlet reporting; Royal Thai Army and Defence Ministry (insurgency link)
record.note: headline only; The Pattaya News reported two people injured and about 24 million baht in valuables taken; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

record.title: Police officer and militant killed in Pattani gunfight
record.detail: Thai Newsroom reported a policeman was killed in a clash with insurgents in Pattani; The Nation reported the gunfight took place at an Islamic school and one militant was shot dead.
record.note: headlines only (Thai Newsroom; The Nation 40056849); Thai PBS World describes the dead officer as a security officer; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

record.title: Bomb at tea shop in Narathiwat kills two
record.detail: A bomb went off at a tea shop in Narathiwat on Thursday 16 October; Thai Examiner reported on 22 Oct that the death toll had risen to two, including an elderly woman. The Nation reported three police and six civilians injured, while The Star reported 14 injured.
record.note: headlines only; injury figures differ between outlets (9 per The Nation, 14 per The Star); Bernama reported a blast injuring 10 in Yi-ngo district that may be the same event; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

record.title: Thailand and BRN agree to resume peace dialogue
record.detail: Malay Mail reported the Thai government and the Patani Malay BRN would resume the southern peace dialogue with Malaysia as facilitator and host; The Nation separately reported a new head of the Thai peace panel held a special meeting with BRN.
record.attribution: Thai government and BRN (via Malaysian facilitator)
record.note: headline only

record.title: SBPAC releases 22-year Deep South toll
record.detail: SBPAC figures based on certified compensation cases counted 10,116 incidents, 5,999 deaths and 13,519 injured from January 2004 to December 2025; 2025 alone had 150 certified incidents and 48 deaths.

record.title: Thai government and BRN meet in Malaysia
record.detail: Prachatai reported the Thai panel led by NIA head Thanat Suwannanon met BRN representatives in Malaysia on 8-9 January 2026 and that the meeting ended badly over BRN demands for self-governance.

record.title: Coordinated bombings hit 11 PTT petrol stations
record.detail: Bombs and fires struck 11 PTT petrol stations within about 40 minutes: five in Narathiwat, two in Pattani and four in Yala. The army and officials reported four injured (a police officer, a firefighter and two station staff); the military imposed a curfew in Narathiwat.
record.place: Multiple sites incl. Ban Khok, Chuap (Cho-airong); Dusongyo (Chanae); Ra-ngae; Waeng; Su-ngai Kolok; Mueang Pattani; Kapho; Kabang; Bannang Sata; Mueang Yala
record.attribution: Thai Army; Narathiwat governor (injury count via The Defense Post)

record.title: Night curfew imposed in Narathiwat after petrol-station attacks
record.detail: Malay Mail reported Thailand imposed an immediate curfew in Narathiwat after a spate of explosions at petrol stations; The Nation reported a 9 pm to 5 am curfew, and The Star reported on 12 Jan that the government had lifted it.
record.note: security response to the 11 Jan petrol-station attacks already recorded; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

record.title: Gunfight as troops move to arrest Yala petrol-station attack suspects
record.detail: Thai Newsroom reported a gunfight erupted when troops cordoned a hideout in Yala to arrest suspects in the petrol-station arson attacks; The Nation reported an alleged insurgent suspect linked to those attacks was shot dead.
record.note: headlines only (also The Star 2026-01-20, The Nation 40061476); province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

record.title: Bomb explodes during assembly in Yala house
record.detail: A device went off inside a house in Moo 1, Ban Yala while it was being assembled, seriously injuring the bomb-maker. ISOC Region 4 Forward Command said parts were linked to an insurgent group.
record.attribution: Internal Security Operations Command Region 4 Forward Command

record.title: Toilet time-bomb wounds EOD officer at Pattani petrol station
record.detail: Timed devices were found in toilets at three PTT stations in Mueang Pattani; the third, at Talubo, exploded during disposal on 4 February and injured a bomb-disposal police officer. Thairath reported the devices were timed for 14 February.
record.place: PTT station, Talubo subdistrict (also Sabarang and Ruesamilae sites)

record.title: Suspected bomb found in Pattani bus terminal restroom
record.detail: A suspected homemade bomb was found in the women's restroom of the Pattani bus terminal and the terminal was evacuated. The Star called it the third such find in three days, after devices at petrol stations.
record.note: also The Star, 5 Feb (https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2026/02/05/suspected-bomb-found-at-bus-terminal-in-thai-province-of-pattani-incident-is-third-in-three-days); coordinates are the town centre

record.title: IED hits army convoy near Ban Wang Hin bridge, Bannang Sata
record.detail: An IED was detonated against a REVA armoured vehicle of a rapid-response infantry unit securing election routes, injuring one soldier; Thairath said an exchange of gunfire followed.
record.place: Ban Wang Hin bridge, Ban Tue-ra

record.title: Culvert gas-cylinder bomb misses police, hurts three villagers
record.detail: A roughly 50 kg gas-cylinder bomb planted in a road culvert exploded as a police vehicle passed but hit a civilian pickup behind it, injuring three villagers. Authorities blamed insurgents trying to ambush police.

record.title: Seven overnight bombs hit shops in Yi-ngo and Ra-ngae
record.detail: Seven small bombs exploded between 23:00 on 14 February and 05:00 on 15 February at shops and a house in Yi-ngo and at two sites in Tanyong Mas (Ra-ngae). No injuries were reported.
record.place: Five sites in Yi-ngo; two in Tanyong Mas

record.title: ISOC Region 4 detains 11 over PTT petrol-station arson
record.detail: ISOC Region 4 said it had detained 11 suspects over the January arson and bomb attacks on PTT stations; officials said members of a Narathiwat cell had learned bomb-making online.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Roadside bomb misses prisoner-escort vehicle on Ban Niang–Yaha road
record.detail: A roadside bomb went off on the Ban Niang–Yaha road, apparently aimed at a vehicle carrying a suspect in custody. It missed its target.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Roadside bomb injures two in Bannang Sata
record.detail: Khaosod English reported a roadside bomb injured two people in Yala's Bannang Sata district after spray-painted messages were found in the area.
record.note: headline only; victim category not stated in headline

record.title: Suspect killed in Nong Chik siege
record.detail: Security forces surrounded a house holding a security-case suspect, who fired at a drone and officers and threw an explosive; officials said the suspected insurgent was killed.

record.title: Border patrol policeman and suspect killed in Nong Chik clash
record.detail: A 10-minute firefight in a rubber plantation after security forces surrounded suspects killed a Border Patrol Police officer and one suspected insurgent. The Pattani Task Force commander linked suspects to the 'Wae Aree' network.
record.place: Moo 6, Ban Pakalue Song, Tuiyong subdistrict

record.title: Bomb at Thanam outpost injures five officers
record.detail: An IED left on a motorcycle sidecar exploded outside the Thanam strategic outpost, starting a fire and injuring five officers' hearing. Police said it was likely retaliation for the Nong Chik clashes.
record.place: Thanam outpost, Ban Kha, Thanam subdistrict

record.title: Gunmen fire on Narathiwat MP Kamolsak's vehicle
record.detail: Gunmen in a pickup fired more than 10 rounds at the car of Prachachat MP Kamolsak Leewamoh outside his Bacho home; he was unharmed but his driver and police bodyguard were wounded. Police later identified former military personnel as suspects and HRW reported an ISOC-registered vehicle was used, so this is not an insurgent attack.

record.title: Bomb and fire destroy Mini Big C in Thung Yang Daeng
record.detail: An explosion and fire destroyed a Mini Big C convenience store in Thung Yang Daeng district early in the morning, after it had closed. No casualties were reported.
record.note: date from the supplied 28 Sep 2026 IED review (the source URL carries no date); Khaosod English also posted it; casualties not stated in the headline; coordinates are the district centre

record.title: Father and son arrested over attack on Narathiwat MP's car
record.detail: Police arrested a father and son, both former marines, over the March gun attack on Narathiwat MP Kamolsak's vehicle. Two more suspects were being sought.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Deputy district chief and companion killed in Chanae ambush
record.detail: About eight gunmen fired on a parked pickup at Ban Sue, killing deputy district chief Monchai Jitkamolkarn and a 27-year-old; an M16 was taken. Police said personal motives were also being examined.

record.title: Village headman shot dead in Sai Buri
record.detail: Headman Reeya Salae was shot while riding to dawn prayers and died in hospital; police were considering a personal dispute as well as insurgency.

record.title: 500 local leaders rally against violence after Chanae killings
record.detail: About 500 sub-district and village heads gathered to reject violence and condemn the killing of a senior deputy district chief and a local-administration official.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Four rangers badly wounded in Chanae ambush
record.detail: Gunmen ambushed a ranger unit in Chanae district, seriously wounding four rangers. A company commander led the pursuit.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Region 9 police report 27 arrests in Deep South sweep
record.detail: The Provincial Police Region 9 commander said a sweep had led to 27 arrests. In the case of the attack on the Narathiwat MP, three people had been arrested and two were still being sought.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Suspected bomb found by road and teacher's residence burns in Pattani
record.detail: Thai Newsroom reported a bomb-like object was found beside a road and a teacher's residence caught fire in Pattani.
record.note: headline only; cause of fire not stated; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

record.title: Pattani court jails bombers over Sai Buri attack
record.detail: Pattani Provincial Court sentenced a group of defendants to 10 years and 6 months in prison for a bombing in Sai Buri district.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Intelligence chief named head of southern peace dialogue team
record.detail: Thai Enquirer reported the National Security Council appointed Tanat Suwannanon, director of the National Intelligence Agency, as the new head of the southern peace dialogue team and expanded cooperation with Malaysia; Thai PBS World and the Bangkok Post also reported the appointment.
record.note: date derived from the post's timestamp

record.title: Roadside bomb wounds one officer in Pattani
record.detail: A roadside bomb wounded one officer in Pattani. The supplied review places it on Route 42 in Yaring district and says it damaged a Royal Thai Navy task-force vehicle.
record.note: headline only; date, district, road and unit from the supplied 28 Sep 2026 IED review; coordinates are the district centre

record.title: Suspect arrested over bombing of rangers in Yala
record.detail: Police arrested a suspect in a bomb attack on rangers in Yala. They said the operation followed the law and respected human rights.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Navy captain answers summons in MP shooting probe
record.detail: A navy captain linked to the case of the attack on Narathiwat MP Kamolsak reported to investigators at Narathiwat provincial police. Separately, Justice Minister Tawee said key evidence in the case was still incomplete.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Roadside bomb hits ranger convoy on Highway 4057
record.detail: A roadside bomb struck Ranger Task Force 11 personnel near Nam Khao bridge. The Nation reported one ranger killed and two injured; an earlier Khaosod report said three were injured.
record.place: Road 4057 near Ban Mai Fad, Kayu Khla subdistrict

record.title: Defence volunteer badly wounded by gunmen in Chanae
record.detail: Gunmen pulled up beside a defence volunteer (Or Sor) as he rode home to his quarters in Chanae and shot him. He was seriously wounded.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Police sergeant killed in attack on new Sai Buri police station
record.detail: Gunmen fired on officers at a base beside the unfinished Sai Buri police station; a police sergeant major, 29, died. Officials said it bore hallmarks of insurgent violence. Thai Examiner described it as a 'Friday evening' attack, which matches 22 May; its dateline is 23 May.
record.place: Sai Buri police station compound, Tabing subdistrict

record.title: Hijab-clad gunmen kill teacher outside Yarang school
record.detail: Four attackers dressed as women fired on a police officer's car outside a school, killing his wife, a teacher who was holding their infant, and wounding the officer. ISOC Region 4 condemned the attack as inhumane.
record.place: Near Prasan Wittaya Foundation School, Pong Sta subdistrict
record.attribution: Internal Security Operations Command Region 4 Forward Command

record.title: Life sentence for Panare bombing
record.detail: A court sentenced a defendant in a Panare district bombing case to life in prison. It also ordered more than 3.6 million baht in compensation.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Suspect in Pattani petrol-station bombings arrested in Bangkok
record.detail: A 21-year-old was arrested at Bangkok's central railway station; authorities alleged he acted as a lookout in the February Pattani petrol-station bombings.
record.place: Bangkok Central Railway Station (case: Mueang Pattani)

record.title: Ranger killed in Chanae raid on suspects
record.detail: Suspects linked to the 1 April Chanae ambush fired on security forces during a dawn raid and escaped into forest; one ranger was killed.

record.title: Two suspected insurgents killed in pre-dawn Pattani firefight
record.detail: Thai Examiner reported two insurgents died in a pre-dawn firefight with security forces in Pattani after refusing calls to surrender; Malay Mail reported the two men were suspected members of a separatist movement.
record.note: headline only; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

record.title: Bomb outside school in Yala injures two police and a civilian
record.detail: The Star reported a bombing outside a school in Yala province injured two police officers and one civilian.
record.note: headline only; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

record.title: Arson attack on Pattani solar farm construction site
record.detail: Khaosod English reported assailants broke into a solar power plant construction site in Pattani early on Monday 15 June and set fire to a solar panel storage area, causing damage but no casualties; authorities launched a manhunt.
record.note: The Nation (40067197) reported an armed attack and blast at a Pattani power plant that closed a highway, probably the same incident; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

record.title: Man, 67, shot three times in Cho-airong ambush
record.detail: Gunmen ambushed a 67-year-old man in Cho-airong district and hit him with three shots. Though seriously wounded, he drove off to get help.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Two separate bombings injure police in Yala and Pattani
record.detail: The Star reported two separate bombings injured police officers in Yala and Pattani provinces.
record.note: headline only; two incidents in two provinces, so no coordinates; injury count not in headline; the Yala blast is also recorded on its own at Than To (Bangkok Post), and Bangkok Post reported five police injured in the Pattani blast

record.title: Roadside bomb injures six border patrol police in Than To
record.detail: A bomb hit a Border Patrol Police unit on teacher-protection duty in Yala, injuring six officers, two of them seriously.
record.note: headline only; district and teacher-protection duty from the supplied 28 Sep 2026 IED review; also VietnamPlus; one of the two blasts in The Star's 19 Jun record; coordinates are the district centre

record.title: Bomb under police pickup explodes after child raises alarm
record.detail: A child saw a man at a police vehicle outside Darussadah Mosque; the device attached to the chassis exploded about ten minutes later while waiting for bomb disposal teams. No one was hurt. Investigators blamed insurgent affiliates.
record.place: Outside Darussadah Mosque, Ban Buketa, Lochut subdistrict

record.title: Truck torched on Yala-Betong highway
record.detail: A ten-wheel truck was set on fire near a bridge at Ban Khlong Nam Khun, blocking Highway 410.

record.title: Bomb outside Thung Yang Daeng religious school injures four
record.detail: A bomb exploded outside a religious school (pondok) in Thung Yang Daeng, injuring four people, including two children.
record.note: date and district from the supplied 28 Sep 2026 IED review (the source URL carries no date); also Chiang Rai Times; coordinates are the district centre

record.title: Defence volunteer shot dead after school run in Yarang
record.detail: Volunteer Defence Corps member Abdulloh Yama was killed while returning from taking his child to a tadika school; the motive was under investigation.
record.place: Ban Ton Makham, Mo Mawi subdistrict

record.title: Tak Bai car-bomb defendant jailed after confession
record.detail: Narathiwat Provincial Court sentenced a defendant in a Tak Bai car-bomb case to 5 years and 12 months after the defendant confessed.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Three PT petrol stations bombed in Yala and Pattani
record.detail: About six men in black planted devices that caused explosions and fires at PT stations in Mueang Yala, Sai Buri and Yaring; one person was injured at the Sai Buri station. Authorities suspected insurgents.
record.place: Sateng Nok (Mueang Yala); Pawa (Sai Buri); Piya (Yaring)

record.title: Culvert bomb in Tak Bai injures two Malaysian tourists
record.detail: Khaosod English and The Star reported a bomb blast in Narathiwat's Tak Bai district injured two Malaysian tourists; The Nation described it as a road-culvert blast, and Malaysian police said the pair had entered Thailand legally.
record.note: headline only; part of the same weekend as the PT petrol-station attacks already recorded on 2026-06-28, but a separate incident

record.title: 28 BRN-linked suspects detained in two-month operation
record.detail: The Star reported Thai authorities detained 28 suspects linked to the separatist group BRN during a two-month security operation.
record.note: headline only; figure covers a two-month period across the region

record.title: BRN blames slow peace talks for surge in violence
record.detail: Mizzima reported BRN claimed that slow progress in peace talks was behind a surge of violence in southern Thailand; the New Straits Times reported BRN saying the peace process remained key to resolving the conflict.
record.note: headline only

record.title: Sawmill owner shot dead in Bannang Sata ambush
record.detail: Gunmen ambushed and killed a sawmill owner in Bannang Sata. The mill had been shot at and set on fire several times before.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Malaysia pledges to work with new Thai peace dialogue chief
record.detail: The Star reported Malaysia would cooperate closely with the new Thai peace dialogue chief, Thanut Suvarnananda; Bernama quoted Malaysian minister Mohamed Khaled.
record.note: headline only

record.title: Car bomb explodes outside old Tanyong police station
record.detail: A 70 kg car bomb driven toward the old Tanyong police station exploded, lightly injuring a police officer. The Nation said it was the 68th car bombing linked to the insurgency since 2005; Al Jazeera said it was the first of 2026.
record.place: Old Tanyong police station, Kaluwo Nuea subdistrict

record.title: Five rangers killed in Bukeh Sami checkpoint attack
record.detail: Six to 10 attackers fired at the checkpoint and threw pipe bombs, killing five rangers, wounding five to six civilians and taking rifles. The government called it terrorism.
record.place: Bukeh Sami checkpoint, Tanyong Mas municipality
record.attribution: Internal Security Operations Command; Al Jazeera citing ISOC Region 4 reports 6 injured

record.title: Construction foreman shot dead at Bannang Sata road site
record.detail: Two hooded men on a motorcycle shot dead a construction foreman supervising road repairs. Police said it was part of insurgent efforts to stir unrest.

record.title: Martial law enforced across Narathiwat after checkpoint attack
record.detail: Thai Newsroom and The Star reported martial law was declared in Narathiwat to track down suspects after the 22 July attack that killed five rangers at a checkpoint; The Pattaya News said the Narathiwat task force extended martial-law powers.
record.note: response to the checkpoint attack already recorded on 2026-07-22; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

record.title: Warrants issued for checkpoint and car-bomb suspects
record.detail: ISOC Region 4 Forward Command said warrants were issued for three suspects: one for the Bukeh Sami checkpoint attack and two for the Tanyong car bomb.
record.attribution: Internal Security Operations Command Region 4 Forward Command

record.title: Off-duty police sergeant wounded by four gunmen
record.detail: Four gunmen shot an off-duty police sergeant in the thigh; he returned fire and the attackers escaped by motorcycle and boat.

record.title: Guns from Bukeh Sami checkpoint attack linked to Chanae killing
record.detail: Police said forensic tests showed that some guns used in the 22 July Bukeh Sami checkpoint attack were linked to the earlier shooting of a Chanae deputy district chief.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Thailand suspends peace talks with BRN; September meeting cancelled
record.detail: The Star reported Thailand suspended peace talks with the southern insurgent group and called off a meeting planned in Malaysia for September; Bernama said the Narathiwat attack forced the talks on hold, and Malay Mail (31 Jul) said the attacks prompted Thailand to rethink the dialogue.
record.note: headline only

record.title: Narathiwat residents march for peace as talks stall
record.detail: Thai Examiner reported people in Narathiwat marched to demand peace after the 22 July attack derailed the Malaysia-facilitated talks.
record.note: headline only; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

record.title: Two police killed in Tak Bai shootout during drug operation
record.detail: A suspect opened fire on Tak Bai police during an anti-drug operation near a palm plantation, killing two officers and injuring four. Authorities later linked the group to the Bukeh Sami checkpoint attack.

record.title: Bomb in official vehicle explodes in Dusongyo
record.detail: An IED in an official vehicle exploded at about 18:45, damaging it; authorities said no one was injured.

record.title: Hearing in MP Kamolsak shooting case postponed to 18 Sep
record.detail: Narathiwat Provincial Court postponed the witness examination of six defendants in the case of the shooting at MP Kamolsak's vehicle to 18 September 2026.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Two suspects in Tak Bai police killings shot dead in Sukhirin
record.detail: Police said the two suspects fired first when cornered in a house and were killed. Eleven people were detained for sheltering them, and the network was linked to the Bukeh Sami attack.

record.title: Yarang raid finds guns, contraband cigarettes and 18m baht
record.detail: ISOC Region 4 searched a suspect house in Yarang district and found illegal cigarettes, firearms and more than 18 million baht in cash.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: 51 coordinated attacks across three provinces in one night
record.detail: Between about 20:00 and midnight, attackers carried out arson, bombings and shootings against local government offices, telecom towers, CCTV, power poles and shops; the army said 51 incidents occurred. The Nation counted 34 (14 Yala, 13 Narathiwat, 5 Pattani), and Thai Examiner later cited 78 including two in Songkhla.
record.attribution: Thai military; Lt Gen Norathip Poinok (via The Nation)

record.title: Roadside bomb wounds three civilians in Narathiwat
record.detail: Al Jazeera reported that a roadside bomb in Narathiwat during the night's coordinated attacks wounded two women and a man. The exact site was not given.

record.title: Gunmen torch government vehicles at Ban Rae SAO, Than To
record.detail: During the coordinated attacks, government vehicles were set on fire at the Ban Rae subdistrict administrative office and a telecom tower was set alight at Si Tha Nam.

record.title: Armed men bomb and burn Bang Pu convenience store
record.detail: At about 20:45 at least five armed men cleared a roadside convenience store, fired into the air and left an IED that exploded about 30 minutes later, destroying the building. No casualties were reported.
record.place: Moo 3, Ban Bang Pu, Bang Pu subdistrict

record.title: Explosive damages railway sleepers at Maruebo, Ra-ngae
record.detail: The State Railway of Thailand found concrete sleepers damaged after the overnight attacks and closed the Narathiwat section. Three more blasts followed on Sunday morning in Pattani and Narathiwat, with no injuries.

record.title: At least 15 attackers raid Phoming municipal office
record.detail: At least 15 attackers subdued guards, burned four municipal vehicles and part of the office, and set off an IED near the guard booth. No casualties were reported. Khaosod dated its report 23 August; the raid may belong to the 22 August wave.

record.title: SBPAC/Isranews: 103 incidents in 2026 through July
record.detail: Figures verified with SBPAC and Isranews's southern news centre put incidents at 1,271 from 2017 to 31 July 2026, including 103 incidents and 245 casualties in 2026.
record.attribution: SBPAC; Isranews Agency Southern News Centre

record.title: Narathiwat imposes curfew after wave of bomb and arson attacks
record.detail: The Star and the New Straits Times reported Narathiwat imposed a curfew after multiple bomb and arson attacks across the southern border provinces.
record.note: security response to the 22-24 Aug attacks already recorded; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

record.title: Suspect detained in Cho-airong after 40-site Narathiwat attacks
record.detail: Police detained a man whom CCTV allegedly showed smashing a security camera in Ban Ku Rong; he denied involvement.

record.title: Gunmen bomb 7-Eleven in Mayo
record.detail: Armed men ordered people out of a 7-Eleven, set fuel and an IED that burned the store, and exchanged fire with police as they fled. Officials suspected the BRN.
record.note: Thai Examiner (25 Aug) dates the attack to Monday, 24 Aug

record.title: Southern army chief: two months' warning did not stop the 51 attacks
record.detail: Fourth Army commander Lt Gen Norathip Poinok said the army had general warning for nearly two months that government offices, high-voltage lines, convenience stores and large shops could be attacked, but no precise targets.
record.note: an official's account of prior threat reporting; general warning, not tactical foreknowledge

record.title: Chanae teen badly wounded; family blames army helicopter
record.detail: A teenager in Chanae was seriously wounded. His brother says the shots came from an army helicopter after the teen raised his hands. The army says it flew the helicopter but used no weapons, and a House military committee has raised the case.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Masked gunmen storm Global House store and set off bombs
record.detail: Five masked gunmen cleared the Global House store, planted three devices and left a 50 kg gas-cylinder bomb on a motorcycle sidecar; the explosions caused no casualties.

record.title: Motorcycle bomb hits police pickup on Route 42, Pattani
record.detail: A bomb on a motorcycle went off as a police pickup passed; Thaiger reported the officers were unharmed. Outlets differ on whether the site is in Mayo or Panare district.
record.note: headline only; date and road from the supplied 28 Sep 2026 IED review; district reported inconsistently (Mayo or Panare), so placed between the two

record.title: Bomb and arson attack on Taluban municipal office
record.detail: Attackers bombed and set fire to the Taluban town municipality office in Sai Buri; the Fourth Army commander said they meant to bring the building down. House Speaker Wan Noor visited on 13 Sep; the attack came earlier and its exact date is not in the headlines.
record.attribution: Fourth Army Region commander (per Nation TV headline)
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Two jailed six months over arson of six PTT stations
record.detail: Narathiwat Provincial Court sentenced two defendants to six months in prison over arson attacks on six PTT petrol stations.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Bomb and gun ambush on defence volunteer truck in Sukhirin
record.detail: Insurgents detonated a roadside gas-cylinder bomb under a truck carrying defence volunteers to a boat race and then opened fire, killing two and wounding 16.
record.place: Highway 4115, Ban Barukaya-ing, Rom Sai subdistrict

record.title: Separatists vow to keep fighting as peace talks stall
record.detail: Al Jazeera reported Malay-Muslim separatists in southern Thailand vowed to keep fighting as peace talks stalled; Malay Mail reported the insurgent group was seeking power, not only talks, with Malaysia at the table.
record.note: headline only

record.title: Assistant village headman shot dead in Bannang Sata
record.detail: Gunmen shot an assistant village headman, 42, with a shotgun as he rode his motorcycle. Investigators had not ruled out a personal dispute.
record.place: Ban Kuelong, Moo 2, Taling Chan subdistrict

record.title: Construction vehicles torched and CCTV destroyed on Highway 410
record.detail: Around 02:30 attackers burned tyres, scattered road spikes, destroyed two CCTV cameras and set fire to three construction vehicles and a resident's car. No injuries were reported.

record.title: Appeal court upholds life term for killing of Nong Chik SAO official
record.detail: The Region 9 Appeal Court sentenced a defendant to life in prison for a shooting that killed a Kholo Tanyong SAO official and another person.
record.note: headline/snippet only

record.title: Four sentenced to life over 2022 Pattani bombing
record.detail: Thai Examiner reported four people were sentenced to life imprisonment for a deadly 2022 insurgent bombing in Pattani, with death sentences commuted to life.
record.note: headline only; court ruling about a 2022 attack; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

record.title: Launching crane falls onto express train at Sikhio
record.detail: A crane at a high-speed rail construction site collapsed onto Special Express Train No. 21 (Krung Thep Aphiwat to Ubon Ratchathani); the provincial command centre reported 32 dead and 66 injured among 171 passengers.
record.agency: Nakhon Ratchasima Provincial Incident Command Centre

record.title: Ethyl acetate spill sickens residents in Phra Samut Chedi
record.detail: A solvent transfer at a private company pier was misrouted into the wrong pipeline, contaminating a drainage canal near Khu Sang Market; about 50 residents were evacuated and at least 7 hospitalised, per the report.
record.place: Behind Khu Sang Market, Pak Khlong Bang Pla Kod
record.agency: Local authorities and public health officials

record.title: Construction crane collapses on Rama II road project
record.detail: A crane at an under-construction highway site on Rama II collapsed a day after the Sikhio disaster; police reported two dead and no injuries.
record.agency: Royal Thai Police; Department of Highways

record.title: Scrap shop fire and gas blast injure firefighter
record.detail: A fire at a scrap-buying shop was followed by a gas explosion that threw debris into a firefighter's chest; more than 10 engines controlled the blaze after over an hour, according to the report.
record.place: Ying Charoen alley, Bang Phli Yai
record.agency: Bang Phli Yai SAO fire services

record.title: Fireworks factory blast in Don Chedi
record.detail: A single-storey fireworks factory behind Wat Dong Kra Chao was destroyed in an explosion; one man died and three were injured, per local officials.

record.title: Tower crane arm falls at Asok construction site
record.detail: The arm of a tower crane broke and fell onto workers at a site beside a shopping centre off Sukhumvit Soi 21; two Myanmar workers were injured, one critically.

record.title: Night fire damages Chatuchak Weekend Market units
record.detail: Fire broke out near Gate 1 after closing time and was controlled in about 25 minutes; the count of damaged units rose from 28 to 48, with a short circuit suspected.
record.place: Chatuchak Weekend Market, Kamphaeng Phet 2 Road

record.title: Students rally at Election Commission for vote recount
record.detail: Student and civil society groups protested at the EC headquarters demanding a nationwide recount and the commissioners' resignation; the report describes heated exchanges but no violence.

record.title: Sakaerat wildfire burns about 6,400 rai
record.detail: Fire in Phu Luang Forest Reserve near the Sakaerat research station burned about 6,400 rai of deciduous forest before being controlled by 14 Feb; 21 agencies and helicopter water-bombing were involved.
record.agency: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment

record.title: M3.1 quake in Phan district, Chiang Rai
record.detail: TMD's Earthquake Observation Division reported a magnitude 3.1 quake at 1 km depth felt in several subdistricts; no damage reported.

record.title: Explosive fire at thinner plant in Ban Pho
record.detail: A thinner and flammable-chemical factory caught fire with multiple explosions; authorities said some workers were believed trapped in one building, with casualties unconfirmed at report time.

record.title: M3.0 quake in Mae Suai, felt in Chiang Rai and Chiang Mai
record.detail: The Department of Mineral Resources reported a shallow (2 km) magnitude 3.0 quake on the Mae Lao fault group; no damage reported.

record.title: Wildfires across Chiang Mai mountain districts
record.detail: GISTDA detected 303 hotspots in Chiang Mai on 31 March, with Samoeng and Mae Taeng worst hit; fires spread across Doi Luang and haze blanketed the city.
record.place: Samoeng, Mae Taeng, Phrao and other districts

record.title: Kaeng Krachan fire burns 1,700 rai at Bang Kloi
record.detail: A fire detected on 10 April spread over 1,700 rai in the UNESCO-listed park; officials blamed illegal land clearing.
record.place: Bang Kloi, Huai Mae Phriang subdistrict
record.agency: Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation

record.title: Child electrocuted at Songkran concert stage
record.detail: An 11-year-old boy died after touching a live speaker pole at a Songkran folk-music stage; a 9-year-old girl was also shocked but survived, per the report.

record.title: Fire at electronics factory in Rojana Industrial Park
record.detail: Nearly 100 workers evacuated as fire with at least two explosions hit an electronics materials plant; controlled in about 40 minutes, short circuit suspected.
record.place: Rojana Industrial Park, Khan Ham subdistrict

record.title: Wildfire hotspots hit 2026 high nationwide
record.detail: VIIRS data cited by the report showed 64,689 hotspots from 1–16 April, peaking at 5,384 a day, mostly in conservation and reserved forests in the north.

record.title: Erawan National Park closed over forest fires and PM2.5
record.detail: The park suspended tourism from 13:00 as forest fires pushed 24-hour PM2.5 to 42.9 µg/m³, per the park chief.

record.title: Forest fire near Tha Pong Daeng park contained
record.detail: About 14 rai of dry dipterocarp forest burned near Ban Sop Pong before forestry officials, soldiers and villagers extinguished it in two hours.
record.place: Ban Sop Pong, Pang Mu subdistrict

record.title: Hunting-linked fire burns ~5,000 rai in Kaeng Krachan
record.detail: Park officials said a fire set to drive gaur during poaching spread over about 5,000 rai; a local council member is suspected.

record.title: Freight train hits bus at Asok-Din Daeng crossing
record.detail: A freight train struck a stationary public bus at a level crossing near Makkasan, setting it ablaze; at least 8 were killed and 35 injured, per Al Jazeera.
record.place: Asok-Din Daeng Road level crossing, Makkasan

record.title: Myanmar M5.3 quake sways Bangkok high-rises
record.detail: A M5.3 quake off Myanmar's southern coast (~247 km SW of Mae Sot) was felt in Bangkok high-rises and parts of the north; some buildings including AMLO were evacuated; no damage reported.

record.title: Rooftop fire forces evacuation of Pattaya hotel
record.detail: Fire on the roof of a fully booked 178-room hotel caused a chaotic evacuation; four were hurt, one with burns to about 20% of his body.

record.title: Fire guts plastic packaging factory in Ban Phaeo
record.detail: About 20 fire trucks fought a blaze that destroyed a plastic box production building at a packaging plant; no casualties reported.

record.title: Warehouse fire at Khon Kaen market injures five
record.detail: Fire in a market warehouse storing flammable goods caused fuel-tank explosions; nearly 20 engines responded and damage was estimated up to 10 million baht.

record.title: Illegal dump fire smokes out area beside Pattaya mall
record.detail: A fire at an illegal dumping site next to a mall on Sukhumvit Road produced thick toxic smoke; no casualties reported.
record.place: Beside Index Living Mall, Sukhumvit Road

record.title: Myanmar M4.7 quake felt in Mae Hong Son and Chiang Mai
record.detail: TMD reported a M4.7 quake at 5 km depth about 62 km NW of Pang Mapha, felt in Pai, Mueang Mae Hong Son, Pang Mapha and Chiang Mai districts.
record.place: Felt around Pang Mapha (epicentre in Myanmar)

record.title: M2.9 quake near Mae Sot
record.detail: TMD reported a M2.9 quake at 1 km depth, intensity II near the epicentre; no damage.

record.title: Century-old shophouse slab falls on pedestrian
record.detail: A second-floor concrete slab of a nearly 100-year-old shophouse collapsed onto Rama IV Road near Wat Traimit, killing a pedestrian and damaging vehicles.
record.place: Rama IV Road near Wat Traimit
record.agency: Suan Mali Fire and Rescue Station

record.title: Ammonia leak at ice factory sends 36 to hospital
record.detail: Ammonia leaked during valve maintenance at an ice plant, forcing about 3,000 students from two nearby schools to evacuate; officials ordered checks of all 28 ice factories in the province.

record.title: Lat Phrao music-bar fire, Thailand's deadliest since 2009
record.detail: Fire broke out near midnight at the Rong Beer Na Lat Phrao venue in Chatuchak; the toll rose to 41 by 19 Aug per the Erawan Centre as cited by the report (initial reports: 27 dead, 73 injured).
record.place: Rong Beer Na Lat Phrao, Lat Phrao Road

record.title: Fireworks stockpile explodes at licensed maker's home
record.detail: Fireworks stored in a garage detonated, injuring two and damaging over seven neighbouring houses; the blast was heard 10 km away.

record.title: Old fuel tank explodes during petrol-station demolition
record.detail: An old underground fuel tank being dismantled at a petrol station in front of Samrong Hospital exploded, injuring three; residual vapour suspected.

record.title: Midnight condo fire in Pattaya injures two
record.detail: A fire in a condominium unit injured a foreign tourist and a Thai resident; 12 others had minor smoke inhalation, per the report.

record.title: Major fire at Khlong Thom Center electronics hub
record.detail: Fire spread through the ~4-rai electronics complex and adjacent units overnight with explosions and partial collapses; 10 were injured, mostly volunteer firefighters, with batteries suspected.

record.title: Fatal fire in On Nut commercial building
record.detail: An e-motorcycle short circuit is suspected in a fire at a three-storey building that killed an elderly woman and injured two.

record.title: Oil and chemical leak in Rama 3 drains
record.detail: Oil and chemicals entered drains along Rama 3 Road, creating flammable vapours; BMA warned residents against sparks while the source was investigated.
record.agency: Bangkok Metropolitan Administration; Pollution Control Department

record.title: Protest outside Patong Chabad centre
record.detail: An estimated 300–500 people protested a Rosh Hashanah event, which was cancelled on security advice; no violence reported.

record.title: Rally at BACC over Senate collusion case
record.detail: A large iLaw-organised rally gathered at the Bangkok Art and Culture Centre before the EC ruling; police monitored and no incidents were reported.

record.title: 228 Indians flown home from Mae Sot after Myanmar scam-centre rescue
record.detail: Indian mission in Thailand said 228 Indian nationals rescued from scam centres in Myanmar were repatriated from Mae Sot on a special Indian Air Force flight.
record.attribution: Embassy of India in Thailand via IANS

record.title: Three Chinese who fled Myanmar scam crackdown arrested in Bangkok
record.detail: Police said three Chinese nationals who had entered Thailand via a natural crossing in Mae Sot after fleeing Myanmar were found in a rented room in Bangkok preparing to travel onward; they had overstayed by more than 360 days.

record.title: Thai army shows seized O'Smach scam base with fake police stations
record.detail: Thai military said the O'Smach complex it seized in Cambodia's Oddar Meanchey province held thousands of people and contained 871 SIM cards, dozens of phones, scam scripts and mock police offices imitating Brazil, China and Australia; Cambodia's interior ministry disputed the characterisation.
record.attribution: Royal Thai Army; disputed by Cambodian Interior Ministry

record.title: Chiang Rai governor warns of scam networks in Tachileik and Kings Romans zone
record.detail: Chiang Rai officials cited 771 suspects arrested in a crackdown in the Kings Romans (Golden Triangle) SEZ in Laos and 288 foreign workers arrested for related offences between Oct 2025 and Jan 2026, and warned residents against cross-border job offers and renting out bank accounts.

record.title: Kings Romans / Golden Triangle SEZ
record.detail: Chiang Rai officials described the Kings Romans zone in Laos as a scammer hideout, citing 771 suspects arrested in a recent crackdown there.

record.title: Tachileik call-centre hub
record.detail: Chiang Rai officials identified Tachileik, opposite Mae Sai, as a major call-centre hub.

record.title: Cambodia says 190 scam sites sealed, ~11,000 workers deported
record.detail: Cambodia's anti-scam commission head said 190 locations had been sealed, 173 people arrested and about 11,000 workers deported, citing a Kampot complex with scripts targeting Thai victims and a fake Indian police station.
record.attribution: Cambodia Commission for Combating Online Scams (Chhay Sinarith)

record.title: Mitta Lin Myaing: new scam buildings south of Myawaddy
record.detail: The Irrawaddy reported at least seven new buildings under construction at Mitta Lin Myaing, about 8 km south of Myawaddy, in an area controlled by Karen BGF Brigade 4, citing residents who said scam-related construction traffic was constant.

record.title: 'KK Park 2.0' (Qingsong Park / Thai Hoa Garden) near former KK Park
record.detail: The Irrawaddy reported a site called Qingsong Park or Thai Hoa Garden, about 5 km from the demolished KK Park, with satellite imagery showing 44 structures; workers reportedly call it 'KK Park 2.0'.
record.attribution: Workers and satellite imagery via The Irrawaddy

record.title: Illegal cross-border internet relay dismantled in Mae Sot
record.detail: True Corporation, the police Anti-Online Scam Centre and NBTC dismantled an illegal relay in Mae Tao subdistrict that was transmitting internet signals across the Moei River into Myanmar, after abnormal traffic was detected on 22-25 February.
record.attribution: True Corporation / Royal Thai Police ACSC / NBTC

record.title: UK sanctions operator of Cambodia's '#8 Park' and Xinbi marketplace
